newsitem.title: UK: General Accident up after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: General Accident up after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in British composite insurance group General Accident rose on Tuesday in thin pre-market dealings after the company reported nine-month pretax operating profits in line with expectations.
General Accident shares were marked 3-1/2p or 0.5 percent higher at 711p by 0822 GMT while the overall market was up 0.14 percent. Some 5,000 shares had changed hands.
General Accident reported an 11.4 percent drop in pretax operating profits to 311 million stg in the first nine months. Analysts had forecast profits in a range of 300 million stg to 324 million.
Marketmakers said the results were positive and predicted the stock would rise further.
"The results were reasonably good and it should be onwards and upwards for the shares...we might see some resistance at 715p though," one marketmaker said.
Traders said the insurance sector as a whole in London could be lifted by news of a planned alliance between French insurers Axa and UAP.
Among other insurers in London, Commercial Union was up 3-1/2p at 644p and Royal & Sun Alliance gained 3-1/2p to 418-1/2p.
Kevin Ryan, insurance analyst at Nikko Europe, said General Accident's 22 million stg underwriting profit and the nine million stg profit in the third quarter were encouraging.

"That really marks the company out as the quality UK player. They won't be matched by Commercial Union...The other thing is that the quality of these composites' earnings has improved and they are balancing risk much better," Ryan said.
Ryan said General Accident's third-quarter performance was unexpectedly good.
"I had thought they would lose ground in the third quarter but they actually gained ground," he said.
However analysts were disappointed at the company's performance in Canada.

"The negative story is clearly Canada which dragged down the numbers somewhat...but it's not a serious problem and should not lead to any changes in earnings forecasts or share recommendations," one analyst said, who asked not to be named.
"Normally they have a very good Canadian result, above the market average. But this looks a bit worse," Nikko's Ryan said.
Ryan, who recommends General Accident as a "buy", agreed earnings forecasts were unlikely to be changed significantly.
